candidates.classification: New bounded current first-contract trace within an earlier broad pending route-time question; no historical unique-count change is implied.
candidates.trace: For a generated case, the planner may return WaitForSafeDeparture. When the party is at a settlement, the 60..=one-day wait helper configures an explicit journey-local minute of day derived from the current public party clock plus the wait; it does not perform a settlement rest. The caller then checks medical/departure readiness and revalidates the route at the corresponding configured absolute minute. If that revalidation returns ReadyWithItinerary, the same loop immediately calls configure_safe_departure_itinerary with None. None maps to 08:00 for a daytime itinerary or 20:00 for a night itinerary, and the native itinerary reducer updates the stored start minute when the settlement party has no wilderness anchor. Thus, conditional on a successful explicit time C, a successful ready revalidation and a later accepted default D different from C, the last setter replaces C with D before the selected travel call. Subsequent provisioning, callback/cache ordering, native acceptance and an admitted route where the safety decision differs remain unproven. The initial planner can use optimistic zero fatigue/thermal state for positive candidate waits, but the inspected caller does perform a separate revalidation using the current state for a zero-additional-wait candidate; this finding does not claim that initial forecast alone authorizes travel.
candidates.connected_repair: Carry the selected journey-local start as part of the typed itinerary through revalidation, the final setter and travel; revalidate the exact committed time and do not convert journey-local configuration into personal rest. Preserve role, walking window, nighttime, bounded follow-up and weather authority. After separately authorized implementation, use a case where C differs from both defaults to verify the persisted time and travel projection; do not treat a substring assertion as execution evidence.

candidates.trace: The simulator route preflight obtains its observed start from the maximum visible personal character time and evaluates weather by adding absolute elapsed minutes. For native unplanned case-site travel, the selected journey-local departure is instead placed on an official world-clock day from refresh_clock, and wilderness environmental exposure wraps elapsed time within that anchored day. The native straight-line route also requests weather at this official-day departure. Therefore when those chosen personal and official day/time inputs differ, the forecast and native route or a subsequently reached camp exposure can query weather for different absolute intervals; actual weather values and safety decisions need not differ. For illustration, if personal time is D 23:00 and a proposed local wait is 120 minutes, the simulator candidate is D+1 01:00, while placing that same 01:00 on an official anchor day D yields D 01:00. This isolates the clock distinction and does not claim that 01:00 survives the separate default overwrite. The weather source uses six-hour absolute intervals. The separately recorded planned-movement exposure omission remains material: do not assume this particular travel movement itself applies native weather exposure. Supported clock divergence, route selection, camp reachability and policy remain open.
candidates.connected_repair: Establish the shared journey environment clock authority and derive forecast samples from the same official-day anchor, selected start and wrapping semantics as the native journey, while preserving independent personal clocks, real clipping and the separately tracked movement-exposure repair. Avoid imposing a personal-time wait where only a journey-local clock was intended.
